nodes.label: SERCA2a
nodes.description:
SERCA2a (Sarco/Endoplasmic Reticulum Ca2+-ATPase 2a, encoded by ATP2A2) is a P-type ATPase that pumps Ca2+ from the cytosol into the sarcoplasmic reticulum lumen. It is the dominant SERCA isoform in cardiac muscle and is indispensable for excitation–contraction coupling, myocyte relaxation (lusitropy), and diastolic function. SERCA2a is a direct substrate of the nuclear sirtuin SIRT1, making it a key conduit by which NAD+-dependent deacetylation protects the heart.

## Structure and Mechanism

SERCA2a is a ~110 kDa transmembrane protein embedded in the sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR) membrane. Its catalytic cycle alternates between high-affinity Ca2+-binding (E1) and low-affinity Ca2+-releasing (E2) conformations, driven by ATP hydrolysis at the cytosolic nucleotide-binding domain. The pump sequesters two Ca2+ ions per ATP consumed, establishing the steep Ca2+ gradient required for rapid myofilament relaxation after each contraction. SERCA2a works in concert with phospholamban (PLN), whose phosphorylation relieves inhibition of the pump and further accelerates Ca2+ reuptake. The efficiency of SERCA2a thus determines both contractility (systole) and relaxation (diastole).

## Regulation by SIRT1

SIRT1 directly deacetylates SERCA2a at lysine residue K492, restoring its ATPase activity and Ca2+ uptake capacity. In failing hearts, SERCA2a expression and activity are diminished, contributing to diastolic Ca2+ overload and contractile dysfunction. SIRT1-mediated deacetylation at K492

nodes.label: Lox-1-mediated foam cell formation
nodes.description: SIRT1 activation reduces lectin-like oxidized-LDL receptor-1 (Lox-1)-mediated foam cell formation by suppressing NF-κB signaling in vascular cells. The directionality is SIRT1 upstream of inhibited Lox-1 scavenging of ox-LDL. This limits macrophage lipid loading, a key early step in atherosclerosis. It is a vascular anti-atherogenic action of SIRT1.

nodes.label: VSMC proliferation and migration
nodes.description: SIRT7 regulates vascular smooth-muscle cell (VSMC) proliferation and migration through the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway, limiting the neointimal hyperplasia that drives vascular disease. The directionality is SIRT7 upstream of VSMC quiescence. By restraining VSMC activation, SIRT7 protects against atherosclerotic and restenotic remodeling. It adds a vascular-stability role to SIRT7.

nodes.label: MDL-800
nodes.description: MDL-800 is a bis-benzenesulfonamide prodrug and potent, selective SIRT6 activator (EC50 = 10.3 μM) that stimulates SIRT6 deacetylase activity. The directionality is MDL-800 allosteric activation of SIRT6. It mirrors UBCS039 but with greater potency and cell permeability, mitigating kidney fibrosis and tumor glycolysis. It is a lead chemical tool for SIRT6 biology.

nodes.label: EX-527 (Selisistat)
nodes.description: EX-527 (Selisistat) is the first known selective, cell-permeable SIRT1 inhibitor (IC50 = 0.098 μM) with minimal activity against SIRT2/3. The directionality is EX-527 blocking SIRT1 catalysis. It is used to dissect SIRT1-dependent phenotypes and was explored clinically for Huntington's disease. As a SIRT1 blocker, its effects contrast with STACs like resveratrol.

nodes.label: SirReal2
nodes.description: SirReal2 is a potent SIRT2 inhibitor (IC50 = 0.14 μM) with minimal effects on SIRT1 and SIRT3, exploiting a SIRT2-specific binding pocket. The directionality is SirReal2 blocking SIRT2 deacetylase activity. It is a key chemical probe for SIRT2 biology in neurodegeneration and cancer. Selectivity makes it valuable for isolating SIRT2-specific effects.

nodes.label: Suramin
nodes.description: Suramin, a polyanionic urea derivative, inhibits sirtuins with IC50 values of ~297 nM, 1150 nM, and 22 μM for SIRT1, SIRT2, and SIRT5 respectively, showing relative selectivity for SIRT5 at higher concentrations. The directionality is suramin blocking sirtuin catalysis. Its broad activity limits specificity, but it remains a tool to probe SIRT5. Clinically, suramin is an antiparasitic and anticancer agent with off-target sirtuin effects.

nodes.label: TGF-β1-induced apoptosis and fibrosis
nodes.description: Overexpression of SIRT1 abolishes TGF-β1-induced apoptosis and fibrosis and suppresses CTGF expression in mouse kidney, protecting renal tissue from TGF-β1 insult. The directionality is SIRT1 upstream of suppressed TGF-β1 pathology. This renoprotective action operates via deacetylation of TGF-β pathway components. It supports SIRT1 activation as a strategy against kidney fibrosis.

nodes.label: TGF-β1-induced fibroblast activation
nodes.description: Genetic knockdown and chemical inhibition of SIRT2 attenuate TGF-β1-induced fibroblast activation and MDM2 expression, reducing fibrogenic responses. The directionality is SIRT2 inhibition → less TGF-β1 fibroblast activation. This is unusual because it implies SIRT2 can promote, rather than suppress, fibrosis in this context. It underscores the context-dependence of sirtuin-fibrosis relationships.

nodes.label: pyruvate dehydrogenase E1α
nodes.description: Pyruvate dehydrogenase E1α (PDH E1α) becomes hyperacetylated at Lys385 in tubular epithelial cells after TGF-β1 stimulation and is deacetylated by SIRT3, modulating pyruvate entry into the TCA cycle. The directionality is SIRT3 enzymatic activation of PDH. This links mitochondrial metabolism to TGF-β1-driven kidney injury. It shows SIRT3 buffering metabolic dysfunction during fibrosis.

nodes.label: osteogenic transdifferentiation of VSMCs
nodes.description: SIRT6 suppresses osteogenic transdifferentiation of vascular smooth-muscle cells via repression of runt-related transcription factor 2 (Runx2), limiting vascular calcification. The directionality is SIRT6 upstream of inhibited VSMC osteogenesis. This protects against stiffening of vessels in atherosclerosis and aging. It is a vascular-homeostasis function of SIRT6.

nodes.label: UUO-induced kidney tubulointerstitial inflammation and fibrosis
nodes.description: The SIRT6 activator MDL-800 mitigates unilateral ureteral obstruction (UUO)-induced kidney tubulointerstitial inflammation and fibrosis, validating SIRT6 activation therapeutically. The directionality is MDL-800 → SIRT6 activation → renal protection. This complements other evidence that SIRT6 restrains TGF-β/Smad3 fibrogenesis. It supports SIRT6 as a target for chronic kidney disease.

nodes.label: Regulatory T cells
nodes.description:
Regulatory T cells (Tregs) are a CD4⁺ T-lymphocyte subset that suppresses excessive immune activation and maintains self-tolerance. They counter chronic inflammation and autoimmunity.

## Rapamycin and Tregs

Inhibition of mTORC1 by Rapamycin reduces lymphocyte overactivation and pro-inflammatory cytokines while increasing Treg numbers. The immune effect is dose-dependent: lower doses are immunostimulatory and bias toward Treg expansion, whereas higher doses cause broad immunosuppression ([Zerdka et al., 2025](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12766144/)). This biphasic profile underlies rapamycin's use to restore immune balance in aging.

> [!note] Biphasic dosing
> Low-dose mTOR inhibition favors Treg expansion and vaccine potentiation; high-dose inhibition suppresses immunity.

## Documents

List of documents in the wiki that mention this entity

- Notes rapamycin increases Tregs while reducing inflammatory cytokines.

nodes.label: T helper type 1 cells development
nodes.description: Dendritic-cell SIRT1 knockout drives T helper 1 (Th1) cell development and promotes inflammation, indicating SIRT1 normally restrains Th1 polarization. The directionality is DC SIRT1 upstream of suppressed Th1 differentiation. This tempers cell-mediated inflammatory responses. It demonstrates SIRT1's immunoregulatory role in antigen presentation.

nodes.label: SIRT6 deficiency (macrophages)
nodes.description: SIRT6 deficiency in macrophages increases acetylation and stability of FoxO1, leading to sustained FoxO1 protein and an inflammatory state. The directionality is SIRT6 loss → hyperacetylated, stabilized FoxO1. Because SIRT6 normally deacetylates FoxO1, its absence prolongs FoxO1 signaling. This reveals a macrophage-intrinsic mechanism linking SIRT6 to inflammation resolution.

nodes.label: GLUT2
nodes.description:
GLUT2 (Glucose Transporter 2, encoded by SLC2A2) is a facilitative glucose transporter with low affinity and high capacity for glucose. It is the principal glucose transporter in pancreatic β-cells, hepatocytes, renal tubular cells, and enterocytes. Its high Km (~17 mM) allows it to function as a glucose sensor, equilibrating extracellular and intracellular glucose concentrations over the physiological range.

## Structure & Mechanism

GLUT2 is a 12-transmembrane-helix facilitative transporter of the SLC2A family. Unlike insulin-dependent GLUT4, GLUT2 does not require translocation to the plasma membrane in response to insulin; it is constitutively expressed at the cell surface. Because it is not saturable at normal blood glucose, the rate of glucose equilibration through GLUT2 reports ambient glucose concentration to the cell.

## Physiological Role

In pancreatic β-cells, GLUT2-mediated glucose uptake is the first step in glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (GSIS). Intracellular glucose is phosphorylated by Glucokinase, initiating glycolysis, ATP production, closure of KATP channels, membrane depolarization, Ca2+ influx, and insulin granule exocytosis. In hepatocytes, GLUT2 exports glucose produced by gluconeogenesis and glycogenolysis and imports it after a meal. In enterocytes and renal epithelium, GLUT2 handles basolateral glucose exit and reabsorption.

nodes.label: Preadipocyte differentiation
nodes.description: SIRT5 inhibits preadipocyte differentiation and lipid deposition by activating AMPK and repressing MAPK signaling pathways. The directionality is SIRT5 upstream of suppressed adipogenesis. This keeps progenitors from becoming lipid-laden fat cells. It positions mitochondrial SIRT5 as a negative regulator of fat accumulation.

nodes.label: Autophagosome-lysosome fusion
nodes.description: TFEB is a master transcription factor for lysosomal biogenesis and autophagy that plays a critical role in autophagosome–lysosome fusion and clearance of cargo. The directionality is TFEB upstream of autophagic-lysosomal execution. Because SIRT2 stabilizes TFEB mRNA, SIRT2 indirectly promotes this fusion. It links sirtuins to the terminal degradative step of autophagy.

nodes.label: LDHB
nodes.description:
LDHB (Lactate Dehydrogenase B subunit) encodes the heart-type (H) subunit of lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), a tetrameric enzyme that catalyzes the reversible conversion of pyruvate to lactate with concomitant reduction of NADH to NAD+. LDHB preferentially converts lactate to pyruvate, favouring oxidative metabolism and gluconeogenic flux.

## Structure and Isozymes

LDH is a homo- or heterotetramer composed of LDHA (M, muscle) and LDHB (H, heart) subunits. The five LDH isozymes (LDH-1 through LDH-5) differ in subunit composition. LDH-1 (B4 homotetramer) predominates in heart and brain, tissues reliant on aerobic respiration, whereas LDH-5 (A4) dominates glycolytic muscle and many tumors.

## Mechanism

The reaction pyruvate + NADH + H+ ⇌ lactate + NAD+ is near-equilibrium. The A subunit favors lactate production (Warburg phenotype), while the B subunit favors lactate oxidation to pyruvate, feeding the TCA cycle. Tissue isozyme distribution therefore determines whether lactate is a waste product or a fuel.

## Regulation by SIRT5

SIRT5 deacetylates LDHB at specific lysine residues, enhancing its enzymatic activity beyond normal physiological levels. Hyperactivation of LDHB by SIRT5 shifts the intracellular lactate/pyruvate balance, leading to metabolic stress that triggers excessive autophagy. This non-canonical activation of autophagy contributes to tumorigenesis, providing cancer cells with recycled nutrients and resistance to metabolic stress. The SIRT5–LDHB axis therefore r

nodes.label: SIRT5-mediated deacetylation of LDHB
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: Deacetylation of LDHB by SIRT5 hyperactivates autophagy, accelerating cellular self-digestion and influencing tumor cell survival and metabolism. The directionality is SIRT5/LDHB upstream of autophagic hyperactivation. This can support tumor cell fitness under stress but may also provoke cell-death programs. It exemplifies SIRT5's role at the autophagy–metabolism interface.

nodes.label: Nkx3.2
nodes.description:
Nkx3.2 (also known as Bapx1) is a homeobox-containing transcription factor belonging to the NK family of developmental regulators. It plays critical roles in skeletal development, particularly in the formation of the axial skeleton and craniofacial structures, by regulating chondrocyte differentiation and joint formation. It is also a direct transcriptional target of the longevity-associated deacetylase SIRT6, linking developmental patterning to vascular homeostasis.

## Structure & Domain Architecture

Nkx3.2 is a 304-amino-acid protein characterized by a conserved N-terminal homeodomain (the NK-type helix–turn–helix DNA-binding motif) and a C-terminal transcriptional regulatory domain. Like other NK-family proteins, it binds to consensus TAATNN motif sequences in target gene promoters. The homeodomain confers both sequence-specific DNA binding and cooperative interactions with partner factors that refine its spatial expression pattern during embryogenesis.

## Physiological Function

- Skeletal Development: Essential for ventral vertebral column formation, sclerotome development, and maintenance of intervertebral discs. Loss of Nkx3.2 in mouse models produces axial skeletal defects, including fused or missing vertebrae and joint malformations.
- Chondrogenesis: Promotes chondrocyte differentiation and cartilage formation by activating Sox9-dependent programs and repressing osteogenic competitors.
- Craniofacial Patterning: Contributes to mandibular and middle-ear ossicle de

nodes.label: GATA5
nodes.description:
GATA5 (GATA Binding Protein 5) is a member of the GATA family of zinc-finger transcription factors (GATA1–6) that bind the consensus motif (A/T)GATA(A/G). GATA5 is expressed predominantly in the cardiovascular system, lung, and gastrointestinal tract, where it governs cell-type-specific gene expression during development and adult homeostasis.

## Role in Cardiovascular Development

GATA5 is essential for cardiac morphogenesis and valvulogenesis. It cooperates with GATA4 and GATA6 to regulate genes critical for cardiomyocyte differentiation, septation, and outflow tract development. In zebrafish, gata5 mutations cause cardiac bifida; in humans, GATA5 variants associate with congenital heart defects (atrial septal defects, bicuspid aortic valve).

## Regulation by SIRT6

SIRT6 promotes GATA5 expression at the transcriptional level, thereby protecting the endothelium from injury. SIRT6-dependent upregulation of GATA5 induces a transcriptional programme that suppresses endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EndMT), reduces oxidative stress, and preserves vascular barrier integrity. In models of vascular endothelial injury (e.g., atherosclerosis, hypertension), SIRT6 loss leads to GATA5 downregulation, exacerbated endothelial dysfunction, and accelerated lesion formation.

GATA5 is a risk locus for coronary artery disease and bicuspid aortic valve. SIRT6 activation to maintain GATA5 levels represents a strategy to counter endothelial injury and cardiovascul

nodes.label: Polyphenol stilbene (3,4',5-trihydroxystilbene)
nodes.description: Resveratrol is the polyphenolic stilbene 3,4',5-trihydroxystilbene, a plant defensive compound produced under stress such as pathogen attack or UV exposure. Its chemical structure features three phenolic hydroxyls that confer redox activity and enable binding to sirtuin and phosphodiesterase targets. The directionality is resveratrol as the small-molecule upstream activator of SIRT1. Though a weak direct antioxidant, its biological impact flows mainly through signaling modulation.

nodes.label: Grape skin
nodes.description: Resveratrol is found concentrated in grape skins, where it contributes to the anti-atherosclerotic benefits attributed to red wine consumption. The directionality is dietary resveratrol upstream of vascular protection. Skin content is modest and matrix-dependent, influencing how much reaches circulation. This botanical source motivated the 'French paradox' hypothesis.

nodes.label: Traditional East Asian medicine (Veratrum formosanum)
nodes.description: Resveratrol-containing plants such as Veratrum formosanum have long been used in traditional East Asian medicine, foreshadowing modern interest in the compound. The directionality is the traditional botanical use upstream of contemporary pharmacological study. This ethnobotanical precedent parallels other stilbene-bearing remedies. It is historical context rather than a mechanistic claim.

nodes.label: Endothelial cells from lipid damage
nodes.description: Resveratrol protects endothelial cells from lipid (e.g., oxidized-LDL) damage, helping preserve vascular barrier and nitric-oxide function. The directionality is resveratrol upstream of endothelial protection. This action is mediated through SIRT1/eNOS and antioxidant pathways. It is a foundational vascular benefit supporting resveratrol's cardiovascular reputation.

nodes.label: Vasodilation via nitric oxide synthesis modulation
nodes.description: Resveratrol promotes vasodilation by modulating nitric-oxide synthesis, principally via SIRT1-mediated activation of eNOS. The directionality is resveratrol upstream of NO-dependent relaxation. Improved vasodilation lowers vascular resistance and blood pressure. This is a direct mechanism behind its cardiovascular effects.
nodes.norm_label: vasodilation via nitric oxide synthesis modulation

nodes.label: Platelet aggregation
nodes.description: Resveratrol inhibits platelet aggregation, reducing thrombotic risk and complementing its vascular benefits. The directionality is resveratrol upstream of suppressed platelet activation. This also creates a bleeding-risk caveat when combined with anticoagulants. It is one of several anti-atherothrombotic actions of the compound.

nodes.label: Smooth muscle cell proliferation
nodes.description: Resveratrol inhibits vascular smooth-muscle cell proliferation, limiting neointimal hyperplasia and atherosclerotic plaque growth. The directionality is resveratrol upstream of suppressed VSMC expansion. This restrains the remodeling that narrows vessels. It complements its anti-platelet and vasodilatory effects.

nodes.label: Coronary relaxation
nodes.description: Resveratrol enhances coronary relaxation, reduces ventricular arrhythmias, and inhibits platelet aggregation and smooth-muscle proliferation, collectively protecting the heart. The directionality is resveratrol upstream of improved coronary function. These integrated effects support myocardial perfusion under stress. They reinforce resveratrol's cardioprotective profile.

nodes.label: Ventricular arrhythmias
nodes.description: Resveratrol reduces ventricular arrhythmias in preclinical models, likely via antioxidant, ion-channel, and eNOS-modulating actions. The directionality is resveratrol upstream of reduced arrhythmogenesis. This adds an electrophysiological benefit to its cardiovascular profile. It is observed in animal studies with uncertain human translation.

nodes.label: Glucose metabolism
nodes.description: Resveratrol improves glucose metabolism and reduces LDL while elevating HDL, improving the lipid profile in metabolic models. The directionality is resveratrol upstream of better glycemic and lipoprotein control. These effects are largely SIRT1/AMPK-dependent. Human outcomes are limited by poor bioavailability.

nodes.label: Direct antioxidant (weaker than vitamin C)
nodes.description: Resveratrol is a relatively poor direct antioxidant, weaker than vitamin C or cysteine at scavenging free radicals in vitro. The directionality is that its redox-scavenging capacity is minor. Its biological benefits therefore arise mainly from signaling modulation (SIRT1, AMPK, eNOS) rather than stoichiometric antioxidant action. This corrects the simplistic 'antioxidant' framing of resveratrol.

nodes.label: Anti-viral effects
nodes.description: Resveratrol demonstrates antiviral effects in some experimental systems, though the evidence base is moderate (confidence 0.75) and mechanism-dependent. The directionality is resveratrol upstream of viral inhibition in those models. Potential mechanisms include modulation of host stress and inflammatory pathways. Clinical relevance remains preliminary.

nodes.label: Anti-neoplastic effects
nodes.description: Resveratrol shows anti-neoplastic effects in preclinical models, including cell-cycle arrest and apoptosis induction, though confidence is moderate (0.75). The directionality is resveratrol upstream of suppressed tumor phenotype in those systems. Mechanisms may involve SIRT1, AMPK, and NF-κB modulation. Robust human anticancer efficacy is unproven.

nodes.label: Vasculature
nodes.description: SIRT1 is highly expressed in the vasculature, including endothelial and smooth-muscle cells, positioning it as a central regulator of vascular homeostasis. The directionality is constitutive vascular abundance enabling rapid SIRT1 responses to metabolic and shear stress. This expression pattern underlies its roles in vasodilation, inflammation, and atherosclerosis. Loss of vascular SIRT1 promotes endothelial dysfunction.

nodes.label: Angiogenic activity during vascular remodeling
nodes.description: SIRT1 modulates angiogenic activity during vascular remodeling and growth, influencing endothelial sprouting and vessel stability in a context-dependent manner. The directionality is SIRT1 tuning angiogenic signaling. It can either promote or restrain angiogenesis depending on oxygen and metabolic cues. This reflects SIRT1's integration of stress and metabolic inputs in the vessel wall.

nodes.label: Angiotensin II type 1 receptor expression
nodes.description: SIRT1 downregulates angiotensin II type 1 receptor (AT1R) expression in vascular smooth-muscle cells, reducing angiotensin-II signaling. The directionality is SIRT1 upstream of AT1R suppression. Lower AT1R diminishes vasoconstriction and hypertensive signaling. This contributes to SIRT1's antihypertensive actions.

nodes.label: TIMP3 (tissue metalloproteinase 3)
nodes.description: SIRT1 regulates tissue inhibitor of metalloproteinase 3 (TIMP3), an endogenous inhibitor of matrix metalloproteinases that defends against vascular inflammation and remodeling. The directionality is SIRT1 upstream of TIMP3 regulation. By preserving TIMP3, SIRT1 limits extracellular-matrix degradation and inflammatory infiltration in vessels. This adds a matrix-protective dimension to SIRT1's vascular role.

nodes.label: Nuclear SIRT1 (enhanced by resveratrol)
nodes.source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin System The Holy Grail of Resveratrol?.md
nodes.description: Nuclear SIRT1, enhanced by resveratrol, induces superoxide dismutase in cardiomyocytes, an antioxidant enzyme that suppresses cell death under stress. The directionality is nuclear SIRT1 upstream of SOD induction. This is a cardiomyoprotective output of resveratrol's SIRT1 activation. It complements SIRT1's eNOS and metabolic cardiac actions.

nodes.label: SIRT3-deficient mice
nodes.description: SIRT3-deficient mice develop severe cardiac hypertrophy and interstitial fibrosis when challenged with a hypertrophic stimulus, revealing SIRT3's protective role in the heart. The directionality is SIRT3 loss → pathological cardiac remodeling. This is driven by elevated ROS and impaired mitochondrial function. It mirrors the resistance seen when SIRT3 is overexpressed.

nodes.label: SIRT3-overexpressing mice
nodes.description: Transgenic mice overexpressing SIRT3 are significantly resistant to stimuli-induced cardiac hypertrophy, the inverse of the SIRT3-null phenotype. The directionality is SIRT3 gain → hypertrophy resistance. This protection arises from better mitochondrial ROS control and metabolic flexibility. It validates SIRT3 as a cardiac therapeutic target.

nodes.label: Stimuli-induced cardiac hypertrophy
nodes.description: Transgenic mice overexpressing SIRT3 are significantly resistant to stimuli-induced cardiac hypertrophy, the inverse of the SIRT3-null phenotype. The directionality is SIRT3 gain → hypertrophy resistance. This protection arises from better mitochondrial ROS control and metabolic flexibility. It validates SIRT3 as a cardiac therapeutic target.

nodes.label: SIRT7-deficient mice
nodes.description: SIRT7-deficient mice show extensive myocardial fibrosis, high basal apoptosis, and cardiomyopathy, reflecting SIRT7's role in maintaining cardiac homeostasis. The directionality is SIRT7 loss → fibrotic cardiomyopathy. This contrasts with contexts where SIRT7 promotes fibrosis under stress. It indicates SIRT7 is overall required for myocardial integrity.

nodes.label: Extensive myocardial fibrosis and cardiomyopathy
nodes.description: SIRT7-deficient mice show extensive myocardial fibrosis, high basal apoptosis, and cardiomyopathy, reflecting SIRT7's role in maintaining cardiac homeostasis. The directionality is SIRT7 loss → fibrotic cardiomyopathy. This contrasts with contexts where SIRT7 promotes fibrosis under stress. It indicates SIRT7 is overall required for myocardial integrity.

nodes.label: Red wine matrix
nodes.source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin System The Holy Grail of Resveratrol?.md
nodes.description: Resveratrol achieves efficacious levels only when ingested within the red-wine matrix, which contains co-constituents that slow its metabolism and improve exposure. The directionality is matrix components upstream of better resveratrol bioavailability. This helps resolve discrepancies between in vitro potency and in vivo human trials. It supports whole-food over isolated-compound approaches.

nodes.source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin System The Holy Grail of Resveratrol?.md

nodes.label: ~8–14 minutes
nodes.description: Resveratrol has a very short plasma half-life of roughly 8–14 minutes because of rapid conjugation and clearance. The directionality is rapid metabolism upstream of low systemic exposure. This severely limits the duration of any SIRT1 activation after a single dose. Sustained-release or matrix strategies are needed for durable effects.

nodes.label: Cytochrome P450
nodes.description: Hepatic cytochrome P450 enzymes contribute to resveratrol catabolism, alongside phase-II conjugation, determining its metabolic fate. The directionality is CYP enzymes upstream of resveratrol clearance. This hepatic handling caps bioavailability. It is relevant to drug–drug interactions and dosing.

nodes.label: Cytochrome P450 activity
nodes.description: Resveratrol both is metabolized by and inhibits cytochrome P450 activity, creating a self-reinforcing effect on its own clearance and on co-administered drugs. The directionality is resveratrol upstream of CYP inhibition. This can alter the pharmacokinetics of other medications. It is a clinically relevant interaction caveat.

nodes.label: Quercetin and ethanol
nodes.source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin System The Holy Grail of Resveratrol?.md
nodes.description: Quercetin and ethanol, red-wine constituents, augment resveratrol activity possibly by inhibiting its catabolic enzymes and improving exposure (moderate confidence 0.75). The directionality is these co-compounds upstream of enhanced resveratrol effect. This helps explain the matrix/bioavailability phenomenon. It suggests combination formulations could improve efficacy.

nodes.label: French Paradox
nodes.description: The French paradox describes lower cardiovascular-disease incidence in some French populations despite high-fat diets, often attributed in part to moderate wine (and resveratrol) consumption. The directionality is moderate wine intake upstream of reduced CVD in this epidemiological observation. Causality is debated, with diet and lifestyle confounders. Resveratrol's vascular actions provide a plausible—but not proven—mechanism.

nodes.label: Bleeding risk with concurrent anticoagulant use
nodes.description: Because resveratrol inhibits platelet aggregation, concurrent use with anticoagulants such as heparin or warfarin may increase bleeding risk. The directionality is resveratrol plus anticoagulant upstream of heightened bleeding liability. This is a practical safety caveat for supplementation. Clinicians advise caution in anticoagulated patients.

nodes.label: SIRT1 downregulation of angiotensin II type 1 receptor
nodes.description: SIRT1-mediated downregulation of AT1R expression produces antihypertensive effects; in vivo, resveratrol-driven SIRT1 elevation reduces angiotensin-II-induced hypertension. The directionality is SIRT1/AT1R suppression upstream of lower blood pressure. This couples SIRT1 activation to vascular tone control. It is a mechanistic basis for resveratrol's antihypertensive actions.

nodes.label: Beclin1
nodes.description:
Beclin1 (also known as Atg6 and BECN1) is a key regulatory protein in the initiation and regulation of Autophagy. It functions as a molecular scaffold that assembles the class III PI3K complex, which produces phosphatidylinositol 3-phosphate (PI3P) to nucleate autophagosome formation.

## Structure and Domains

Beclin1 is a 450-amino-acid protein containing several conserved domains:

- BH3 Domain (Bcl-2 homology 3): Mediates interaction with anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 family members (Bcl-2, Bcl-xL, Mcl-1). Binding of Bcl-2 to the BH3 domain sequesters Beclin1 and inhibits autophagy.
- CCD (Coiled-Coil Domain): Mediates homodimerisation and interaction with UVRAG (UV radiation resistance-associated gene).
- ECD (Evolutionarily Conserved Domain): Required for interaction with Vps34 and Vps15, forming the core class III PI3K complex.
- NLS (Nuclear Localisation Signal): Mediates nuclear-cytoplasmic shuttling of Beclin1.

## The Class III PI3K Complexes

Beclin1 is the central scaffold of three distinct class III PI3K complexes:

| Complex | Subunits | Function |
|---------|----------|----------|
| Complex I | Beclin1-Vps34-Atg14L-Vps15/p150 | Autophagosome nucleation |
| Complex II | Beclin1-Vps34-UVRAG-Vps15/p150 | Autophagosome maturation and endocytosis |
| Complex III | Beclin1-Vps34-UVRAG-Rubicon-Vps15/p150 | Suppresses autophagosome maturation |
| Complex IV | Beclin1-Vps34-UVRAG-Bax-interacting factor 1 (Bif-1) | Promotes autophagosome formation |

nodes.label: FoxO1 (pancreatic β cells)
nodes.description: In pancreatic β-cells, SIRT6 deacetylates FoxO1 and increases GLUT2 expression to maintain glucose-sensing ability and systemic glucose tolerance. The directionality is SIRT6 enzymatic activation of FoxO1 in β-cells. This preserves insulin secretory competence under metabolic challenge. It mirrors SIRT6's broader metabolic-protective phenotype.

nodes.label: Nrf2 (via Keap1 modification)
nodes.description: SIRT1 activates Nrf2 by modifying Keap1 structure, leading to Nrf2 nuclear translocation and expression of antioxidant genes. The directionality is SIRT1 upstream of Nrf2 activation. This is a canonical cytoprotective axis against oxidative and electrophilic insult. It complements SIRT1's direct antioxidant substrate actions.

nodes.label: CPS1
nodes.description:
Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthase 1 (CPS1) is a mitochondrial enzyme that catalyzes the first and rate-limiting step of the urea cycle, converting ammonia and bicarbonate into carbamoyl phosphate. Ammonia is a highly toxic byproduct of amino acid catabolism, and its clearance via conversion into urea in the liver is essential for cellular and systemic health.

## Metabolic Role and Urea Cycle

CPS1 is primarily expressed in hepatocytes and intestinal mucosal cells. Within the mitochondrial matrix, CPS1 combines ammonium ($NH_4^+$), bicarbonate ($HCO_3^-$), and two molecules of ATP to form carbamoyl phosphate. This product then enters the urea cycle by condensing with ornithine to form citrulline, facilitated by ornithine transcarbamylase (OTC).

## Regulation by SIRT5-Mediated Desuccinylation

In the mitochondria, CPS1 activity is highly regulated by post-translational modifications, particularly succinylation on multiple lysine residues:
- Succinylation Inhibits CPS1: Lysine succinylation (the addition of a negatively charged succinyl group) on CPS1 disrupts its active site conformation and severely reduces its catalytic activity.
- SIRT5 Restores Activity: SIRT5, a mitochondrial NAD⁺-dependent desuccinylase, demalonylase, and deglutarylase, binds to CPS1 and removes these succinyl marks (specifically at lysine residue K1291).
- Metabolic Coordination: Under fasting, caloric restriction, or high-protein diet conditions, amino acid catabolism increases, generating excess ammonia.

nodes.label: NLRP3 inflammasome (via AMPKα/XBP1)
nodes.description: SIRT1 protects against inflammation by deacetylating and attenuating NLRP3 activity via the AMPKα/XBP1 pathway in macrophages. The directionality is SIRT1 enzymatic suppression of NLRP3 through XBP1s. This couples ER-stress responses to innate immune regulation. It is a refined mechanistic view of SIRT1's anti-inflammasome action.

nodes.label: Heart failure (via SERCA2a deacetylation)
nodes.description: SIRT1 deacetylates SERCA2a at Lys492, restoring its activity and improving cardiac contractility in heart failure. The directionality is SIRT1 enzymatic rescue of SERCA2a. Better calcium handling opposes the systolic dysfunction of failure. This is a direct mechanistic rationale for SIRT1 activation in cardiomyopathy.

nodes.label: TGF-β1/Smad3 signaling
nodes.description: SIRT6 prevents TGF-β1-induced lung myofibroblast differentiation by inactivating TGF-β1/Smad3 signaling, limiting fibrogenesis. The directionality is SIRT6 upstream of TGF-β1/Smad3 blockade. This complements SIRT6's other antifibrotic actions in heart and kidney. It positions SIRT6 as a broad suppressor of Smad3-driven fibrosis.

nodes.label: MFN2 (at K655, K662)
nodes.description: SIRT1 deacetylates mitofusin 2 (MFN2) at Lys655 and Lys662, regulating mitochondrial fusion and quality control; loss of SIRT1 causes defective autophagy linked to impaired MFN2 function. The directionality is SIRT1 enzymatic modification of MFN2. This connects sirtuin activity to mitochondrial dynamics and mitophagy. It is relevant to neurodegenerative and metabolic disease where fusion is perturbed.

nodes.label: p53 at Lys379
nodes.description: SIRT1 deacetylates p53 specifically at Lys379, inhibiting p53-dependent apoptosis and promoting cell survival under genotoxic stress. The directionality is SIRT1 enzymatic inactivation of p53 at this site. This is one of several lysines (including Lys317/370) targeted by SIRT1. The net effect is cytoprotection that can be oncogenic in established tumors.

nodes.label: AMPK (preadipocyte differentiation)
nodes.description: SIRT5 inhibits preadipocyte differentiation by activating AMPK and repressing MAPK signaling, analogous to its broader adipogenesis-blocking role. The directionality is SIRT5 upstream of AMPK activation in adipogenic progenitors. Activated AMPK shifts cells away from lipogenesis. It reaffirms SIRT5 as a negative regulator of fat formation.

nodes.label: Nicotinamide to NMN
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: NAMPT condenses nicotinamide with 5-phosphoribosyl-1-pyrophosphate (PRPP) to form NMN, the rate-limiting step of the NAD+ salvage pathway. The directionality is NAMPT upstream of NMN/NAD+ biosynthesis. This recovers nicotinamide that would otherwise feedback-inhibit sirtuins. AMPK and SIRT1 both induce NAMPT, creating a positive loop for NAD+ and sirtuin activity.

nodes.label: TGF-beta1
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: TGF-β1 binds the type II receptor (TβRII), which recruits and phosphorylates the type I receptor (TβRI), leading to phosphorylation and nuclear translocation of SMAD2/3 to drive fibrotic transcription. The directionality is TGF-β1 upstream of SMAD3 activation. This canonical pathway is the main driver of pathological fibrosis across organs. Sirtuins such as SIRT6 and SIRT7 intersect this axis at multiple points.

nodes.label: SMAD3
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: TGF-β1 binds the type II receptor (TβRII), which recruits and phosphorylates the type I receptor (TβRI), leading to phosphorylation and nuclear translocation of SMAD2/3 to drive fibrotic transcription. The directionality is TGF-β1 upstream of SMAD3 activation. This canonical pathway is the main driver of pathological fibrosis across organs. Sirtuins such as SIRT6 and SIRT7 intersect this axis at multiple points.

nodes.label: Pathological fibrosis
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: TGF-β1 activates SMAD3-dependent transcription of pro-fibrotic genes (COL1A1, COL3A1, FN1, ACTA2, TIMP1), driving collagen deposition and tissue scarring in multiple organs. The directionality is TGF-β1 upstream of fibrogenesis. This makes TGF-β1 a central target in fibrosis therapeutics. Sirtuins that inhibit SMAD3 signaling (SIRT6, SIRT7) are antifibrotic.

nodes.label: BRCA1
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: BRCA1 is recruited to DNA double-strand breaks by the MRN complex, promotes end resection, and facilitates RAD51 loading via PALB2/BRCA2 to execute homologous recombination repair. The directionality is BRCA1 upstream of high-fidelity DSB repair. Loss of BRCA1 cripples HR, increasing mutation and cancer risk. Sirtuins such as SIRT2 support BRCA1 localization to damage sites.

nodes.label: BRCA1 deficiency
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: Loss of BRCA1 triggers increased autophagy as a compensatory survival mechanism in breast and ovarian cancers, buffering the viability impact of defective homologous recombination. The directionality is BRCA1 deficiency upstream of autophagic upregulation. This metabolic rewiring can be co-opted by tumors. It connects genome-maintenance failure to lysosomal clearance pathways.

nodes.label: BRCA1 mutation
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: BRCA1-deficient tumors are exquisitely sensitive to PARP inhibitors because blocking base-excision (PARP) repair in the setting of defective homologous recombination causes catastrophic, lethal DNA damage (synthetic lethality). The directionality is BRCA1 mutation upstream of PARP-inhibitor vulnerability. This is a cornerstone of precision oncology. It illustrates how repair-pathway context determines therapeutic selectivity.

nodes.label: Caspase-3 (at Ser150)
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: p38 MAPK phosphorylates caspase-3 at Ser150, suppressing its proteolytic activity; this inhibition is reversed by the phosphatase PP2A. The directionality is p38 upstream of caspase-3 inhibition. This provides a survival signal that tempers apoptosis under certain stresses. It shows stress kinases can directly restrain executioner caspases.

nodes.label: ULK1, ATG13, FIP200, ATG101
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: ULK1 functions within a stable initiation complex containing ATG13, FIP200 (RB1CC1), and ATG101, which nucleates autophagosome formation in response to nutrient status. The directionality is the complex upstream of autophagy initiation. SIRT1 deacetylates and activates ULK1 within this complex. This positions sirtuins at the top of the autophagic machinery.

nodes.label: ULK1 (at Ser757)
nodes.description: Under nutrient-rich conditions, mTORC1 phosphorylates ULK1 at Ser757, disrupting its interaction with AMPK and suppressing autophagy. The directionality is mTORC1 upstream of ULK1 inhibition. This couples nutrient abundance to autophagic restraint. Sirtuin/AMPK activation opposes mTORC1 to relicense ULK1.

nodes.label: STRAD and MO25 for activity
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: LKB1 requires binding to STRAD and MO25 to exit the nucleus and gain full kinase activity; without this scaffold it remains inactive. The directionality is STRAD/MO25 upstream of LKB1 activation. SIRT1/AMPK deacetylate/phosphorylate LKB1 to modulate its localization. This gating is essential for LKB1's role as the master AMPK kinase.

nodes.label: Thr172
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: LKB1 is the primary upstream kinase phosphorylating AMPK at Thr172 in the activation loop, increasing AMPK activity over a hundred-fold. The directionality is LKB1 upstream of AMPK activation. This couples energy sensing to metabolic reprogramming. Sirtuins feed into this node via LKB1 deacetylation and AMPK-dependent NAD+ elevation.

nodes.label: LKB1 deficiency
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: Germline loss-of-function mutations in STK11 (LKB1) cause Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, characterized by hamartomatous polyps and elevated cancer risk. The directionality is LKB1 deficiency upstream of this cancer predisposition. This highlights LKB1 as a critical tumor suppressor and metabolic regulator. Its connection to AMPK/sirtuin axes explains the metabolic features.

nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

The directionality is Beclin1 upstream of autophagosome machinery assembly. SIRT1 deacetylates Beclin1 to enhance Vps34 activity. This makes Beclin1 a hub integrating sirtuin signals into autophagy.

nodes.label: Tumour suppressor (glutamine metabolism)
nodes.description: SIRT4 acts as a tumor suppressor by inhibiting GDH and restricting glutamine-derived anaplerosis into the TCA cycle, starving cancer cells of carbon for proliferation. The directionality is SIRT4 upstream of suppressed glutamine metabolism. This limits the glutamine addiction of tumors. It is a context where SIRT4 opposes, rather than promotes, growth.

nodes.label: MTPα (fatty acid oxidation)
nodes.description: SIRT4 suppresses fatty-acid oxidation in liver by inhibiting the mitochondrial trifunctional protein α subunit (MTPα), promoting lipid accumulation under nutrient-replete conditions. The directionality is SIRT4 upstream of reduced β-oxidation. This contrasts with SIRT3/SIRT5, which support fat oxidation. It positions SIRT4 as a mitochondrial anabolic brake.

nodes.label: H3K18ac
nodes.description:
H3K18ac is the acetylation of histone H3 at lysine 18, a mark associated with active enhancers, promoters, and p300-target regions. In senescence, H3K18ac is one of the acetyl marks enriched at senescence-activated super-enhancers that drive Senescence-Associated Secretory Phenotype gene expression, as reviewed in the npj Aging survey (Dasgupta et al., 2024; https://doi.org/10.1038/s41514-024-00172-2).

## Definition

H3K18ac neutralizes the lysine positive charge, loosening chromatin and providing a binding surface for bromodomain readers. It is often co-deposited with other enhancer acetyl marks and is a readout of p300/CBP activity at active regulatory elements.

## Writer, Reader, Eraser

- Writer: p300/CBP histone acetyltransferases install H3K18ac at active enhancers and SEs.
- Reader: Bromodomain-containing proteins, including BRD4 and other BET-family members, recognize acetylated lysines.
- Eraser: Class I/IIa HDACs remove the mark.

## Role in SASP and Senescence

Senescence-activated super-enhancers are enriched in H3K4me1 and multiple histone acetyl marks — H3K27ac, H3K18ac, H3K122ac, and H4K5ac (Sen et al., 2019, PMID 30753809). These SEs actively transcribe enhancer RNAs, recruit P300, and directly drive senescence-specific gene expression, including key SASP factors. H3K18ac therefore contributes to the open, transcriptionally competent state of SASP enhancers and cooperates with the AP-1 pioneer factor and BRD4 reader to sustain SASP output.

nodes.label: Replicative lifespan
nodes.description: Overexpression of SIRT7 extends the replicative lifespan of primary human cells by maintaining rDNA stability and reducing mitochondrial dysfunction. The directionality is SIRT7 gain upstream of prolonged cellular lifespan. This mirrors the pro-longevity roles of other sirtuins. It supports a broadly conserved lifespan-promoting function for the family.

nodes.label: 1.5 to 3 mg per liter
nodes.description: Typical red wine contains 1.5–3 mg/L trans-resveratrol (up to ~5.8 mg/L in some cool-climate wines), with a 5-ounce glass providing only ~0.3 mg. The directionality is wine content upstream of modest resveratrol intake. This low dose highlights why drinking alone may not reach pharmacologic exposures. It contextualizes the 'French paradox' and matrix-bioavailability discussion.

nodes.label: 0.15 to 1.3 mg per 100g
nodes.description: Raw red grapes contain roughly 0.15–1.3 mg resveratrol per 100 g, mostly in the skins, making dietary intake from fruit modest. The directionality is grape content upstream of limited resveratrol exposure. Skin concentration explains why wine, not flesh, carries most of the compound. It reinforces that supplementation, not diet alone, reaches high doses.

nodes.label: Vine Tea (Ampelopsis grossedentata)
nodes.description: Vine tea (Ampelopsis grossedentata) leaves contain 20–30% dihydromyricetin (DHM) by weight, so 1–1.5 g dry leaf suffices for a ~300 mg therapeutic dose. The directionality is botanical source upstream of DHM availability. DHM is a potent SIRT3/AMPK activator. This makes vine tea a practical natural source of the compound.

nodes.label: Cyanidin-3-glucoside
nodes.description: Black elderberries provide roughly 350–450 mg cyanidin-3-glucoside per 100 g fresh fruit, with ~70–85 g reaching a 300 mg therapeutic dose. The directionality is berry content upstream of anthocyanin intake. Cyanidin is a powerful natural SIRT6 activator. It positions elderberry as a dietary SIRT6-modulating food.

nodes.label: 350 to 450 mg per 100g
nodes.description: Black elderberries provide roughly 350–450 mg cyanidin-3-glucoside per 100 g fresh fruit, with ~70–85 g reaching a 300 mg therapeutic dose. The directionality is berry content upstream of anthocyanin intake. Cyanidin is a powerful natural SIRT6 activator. It positions elderberry as a dietary SIRT6-modulating food.

nodes.label: Water
nodes.description: Honokiol is highly lipophilic with very poor water solubility, so hot-water tea extraction is inefficient and ethanol tinctures or supercritical CO2 extracts are needed for therapeutic dosing. The directionality is physicochemical property upstream of formulation requirement. Its lipophilicity also aids cell and mitochondrial membrane penetration, supporting SIRT3 engagement. This is a practical caveat for honokiol use.

nodes.label: Dual mechanism (direct + indirect)
nodes.description: Resveratrol activates SIRT1 through both direct allosteric binding at the NTD (Glu230) and an indirect cascade via PDE4/cAMP/Epac1/Ca2+/CaMKKβ/AMPK/NAMPT/NAD+. The directionality is resveratrol upstream of dual SIRT1 activation. The indirect limb raises NAD+ to fuel SIRT1, amplifying the direct effect. This dual mechanism explains resveratrol's robust pleiotropic metabolic benefits.

nodes.label: Tenovin-6
nodes.description: Tenovin-6 inhibits SIRT2 with IC50 = 10 µM, making SIRT2 its more potent sirtuin target compared with SIRT1. The directionality is Tenovin-6 blocking SIRT2 catalysis. By inhibiting SIRT2 deacetylation, it can protect neurons and reactivate p53. It is a chemical probe distinguishing SIRT2 from other sirtuins.

nodes.label: Tenovins
nodes.description: By inhibiting SIRT1/SIRT2-mediated deacetylation, Tenovins promote p53 hyperacetylation and reactivation of p53-dependent transcriptional networks. The directionality is Tenovin-mediated sirtuin inhibition upstream of p53 activation. This restores p53 tumor-suppressive function in cells where sirtuins silence it. It is the basis for Tenovins' anticancer activity.

nodes.label: p53 (via hyperacetylation)
nodes.description: By inhibiting SIRT1/SIRT2-mediated deacetylation, Tenovins promote p53 hyperacetylation and reactivation of p53-dependent transcriptional networks. The directionality is Tenovin-mediated sirtuin inhibition upstream of p53 activation. This restores p53 tumor-suppressive function in cells where sirtuins silence it. It is the basis for Tenovins' anticancer activity.

nodes.label: Xenograft models
nodes.description: Tenovin-1 and Tenovin-6 significantly delay tumor growth in human cancer mouse xenografts (BL2 and ARN8) at single-digit micromolar concentrations. The directionality is Tenovin treatment upstream of reduced tumor growth. This effect is attributed to p53 reactivation and sirtuin inhibition. It validates sirtuin inhibition as an anticancer strategy in p53-wild-type tumors.

nodes.label: Splitomicin
nodes.description: Splitomicin inhibits human SIRT1 with IC50 = 96 µM in vitro by blocking NAD+-dependent deacetylation. The directionality is Splitomicin upstream of SIRT1 inhibition. It is an early-tool sirtuin inhibitor used to probe SIRT1 phenotypes. Its moderate potency limits in vivo utility.

nodes.label: NF-κB p65
nodes.description: Splitomicin reduces intracellular deacetylase activity, causing hyperacetylation and enhanced nuclear translocation of NF-κB p65, amplifying inflammatory transcription. The directionality is Splitomicin (sirtuin inhibition) upstream of increased NF-κB signaling. This demonstrates the converse of SIRT1's normal anti-inflammatory action. It shows experimentally that sirtuin tone sets inflammatory set-points.

nodes.label: Ischemic preconditioning cardioprotection
nodes.description: In ischemic-preconditioning models, Splitomicin reverses protective lysine deacetylation and abolishes preconditioning-induced cardioprotection. The directionality is Splitomicin (sirtuin inhibition) upstream of lost cardiac protection. This indicates sirtuin deacetylase activity is required for ischemic tolerance. It argues that sirtuin activation, not inhibition, protects the heart.

nodes.label: Cambinol
nodes.description: Cambinol inhibits human SIRT1 with IC50 = 56 µM by blocking access to both NAD+ and acetyl-lysine substrate-binding regions. The directionality is Cambinol upstream of SIRT1 inhibition. It also inhibits SIRT2, with minimal activity against SIRT3 or class I/II HDACs. Cambinol sensitizes cancer cells to chemotherapy and suppresses invasion.

nodes.label: Cancer cell migration and invasion
nodes.description: In hepatocellular and lung cancer cells, Cambinol impairs migration and invasion in a dose-dependent manner, consistent with sirtuin inhibition reducing metastatic behaviors. The directionality is Cambinol upstream of suppressed motility. This suggests sirtuin blockers may limit metastasis. It complements Cambinol's chemotherapy-sensitizing effects.

nodes.label: Cancer cells to chemotherapy
nodes.description: Cambinol combination with chemotherapeutic agents dramatically sensitizes cancer cells to chemotherapy-induced apoptosis. The directionality is Cambinol upstream of enhanced chemosensitivity. By inhibiting SIRT1/2, it removes survival signals that protect tumor cells. This supports sirtuin inhibition as a chemosensitization strategy.

nodes.label: Salermide
nodes.description: Salermide is a potent synthetic sirtuin inhibitor with improved potency against SIRT1 relative to the parent compound sirtinol. The directionality is Salermide blocking SIRT1 deacetylase activity. This reactivates proapoptotic genes silenced by SIRT1 in cancer. It is a research and anticancer chemical probe.

nodes.label: Proapoptotic genes (via H4K16ac)
nodes.description: Salermide inhibits SIRT1-mediated deacetylation of H4K16, leading to epigenetic reactivation of proapoptotic genes aberrantly repressed in cancer cells. The directionality is Salermide → H4K16 hyperacetylation → apoptosis gene expression. This removes a chromatin-based survival brake. It is a mechanistic rationale for sirtuin-inhibitor cancer therapy.

nodes.label: Cancer cell lines (MOLT4, MDA-MB-231, RKO)
nodes.description: Salermide induces robust apoptosis in leukemia (MOLT4), breast (MDA-MB-231), and colon (RKO) cancer cells, validating broad antitumor activity. The directionality is Salermide treatment upstream of cancer-cell death. This is consistent with SIRT1/2 inhibition removing survival signaling. It supports sirtuin blockers as anticancer agents.

nodes.label: Colorectal cancer stem cells
nodes.description: Salermide inhibits colorectal carcinoma cancer-stem-cell self-renewal and reduces tumorigenesis, targeting the resilient stem-cell fraction. The directionality is Salermide upstream of stem-cell suppression. This is important because stem cells drive relapse. It extends sirtuin-inhibitor effects to the tumor-initiation compartment.

nodes.label: Sirtinol
nodes.description: Sirtinol inhibits SIRT1 with IC50 ≈ 131 µM, preventing deacetylation of histones and non-histone targets. The directionality is Sirtinol upstream of SIRT1 inhibition. It is the parent compound of salermide and a classic sirtuin research tool. Its weaker potency spurred development of derivatives like salermide.

nodes.label: Senescence-like growth arrest
nodes.description: Sirtinol induces senescence-like growth arrest in human lung cancer H1299 cells, consistent with sirtuin inhibition engaging tumor-suppressive programs. The directionality is Sirtinol upstream of growth arrest. This phenotype mirrors aspects of SIRT1 loss. It suggests sirtuin blockers can blunt proliferation.

nodes.label: Apoptotic and autophagic cell death (MCF-7)
nodes.description: In MCF-7 breast cancer cells, sirtinol triggers both apoptotic and autophagic programmed cell death, reflecting disrupted survival homeostasis. The directionality is Sirtinol upstream of dual cell-death activation. This is attributed to SIRT1/2 inhibition removing anti-apoptotic deacetylation. It illustrates the pleiotropic anticancer potential of sirtuin blockers.

nodes.label: CD38 inhibitor 78c
nodes.description: 78c is a highly potent, selective, orally bioavailable small-molecule inhibitor of CD38 NAD+-glycohydrolase activity. The directionality is 78c upstream of CD38 blockade. By stopping NAD+ consumption, it spares the co-substrate for sirtuins. This is a leading age-reversal NAD+-preservation strategy.

nodes.label: CD38 (NAD+-glycohydrolase)
nodes.description: 78c is a highly potent, selective, orally bioavailable small-molecule inhibitor of CD38 NAD+-glycohydrolase activity. The directionality is 78c upstream of CD38 blockade. By stopping NAD+ consumption, it spares the co-substrate for sirtuins. This is a leading age-reversal NAD+-preservation strategy.

nodes.label: NAD+ levels
nodes.description: By selectively inhibiting CD38, 78c prevents age-related NAD+ degradation, keeping cellular pools high in aged animals. The directionality is CD38 inhibition upstream of preserved NAD+. Higher NAD+ then fuels sirtuin and other NAD+-dependent enzymes. This reverses a hallmark of aging.

nodes.label: Sirtuin activity (SIRT1, SIRT3)
nodes.description: 78c indirectly boosts SIRT1 and SIRT3 by maintaining NAD+ co-substrate availability, restoring their deacetylase function in aged tissue. The directionality is NAD+ preservation upstream of sirtuin reactivation. This is an indirect 'pan-sirtuin' approach distinct from direct STACs. It links CD38 pharmacology to longevity pathways.

Administration of 78c to naturally aged male mice yields about a 14% lifespan extension, demonstrating in vivo geroprotective efficacy. The directionality is CD38 inhibition upstream of prolonged lifespan. This effect is attributed to restored NAD+/sirtuin function. It validates CD38 as a longevity drug target.

nodes.label: NMN and NR
nodes.description: 78c enhances the efficacy of NAD+ precursors NMN and NR by preventing their rapid CD38-mediated degradation, combining supply and preservation. The directionality is 78c + precursors upstream of amplified NAD+ and sirtuin activation. This synergy is a rational anti-aging combination. It overcomes the limited durability of precursors alone.

nodes.label: Fucoidan
nodes.description: Fucoidan (notably Fucoidan-FV) activates SIRT6 by increasing its protein abundance and enhancing its mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase activity. The directionality is fucoidan upstream of SIRT6 activation. Unlike most SIRT6 activators, it preferentially stimulates the ADP-ribosyltransferase function. This yields antifibrotic and LINE-1-suppressing effects.

nodes.label: LINE-1 expression (HGPS fibroblasts)
nodes.description: Fucoidan-FV (50–100 µg/mL) reduces LINE-1 ORF1p and ORF2p protein levels in Hutchinson-Gilford progeria (HGPS) patient-derived fibroblasts, indicating suppressed retrotransposition. The directionality is fucoidan/SIRT6 upstream of LINE-1 silencing. This addresses a progeria-associated chromatin defect. It supports SIRT6 in repetitive-element control.

nodes.label: Healthspan and lifespan (aged mice)
nodes.description: SIRT6-activating fucoidan extends healthspan and lifespan in aged wild-type mice, confirming in vivo geroprotection. The directionality is fucoidan upstream of improved survival and function. This mirrors the longevity association of centenarian SIRT6 variants. It positions fucoidan as a natural SIRT6-targeted intervention.

nodes.label: ML385
nodes.description: ML385 binds the NRF2 bZIP domain, blocking its heterodimerization with small Maf proteins and preventing ARE-driven antioxidant transcription. The directionality is ML385 upstream of NRF2 inhibition. Because SIRT1 activates NRF2, ML385 can be used to disrupt that axis experimentally. It is a tool to dissect NRF2-dependent cytoprotection.

nodes.label: AGK2
nodes.description: AGK2 is a highly selective SIRT2 inhibitor (IC50 = 3.5 µM) with over 10-fold selectivity over SIRT1 and SIRT3. The directionality is AGK2 blocking SIRT2. Its selectivity makes it the preferred probe for SIRT2-specific biology. It rescues neurons in Parkinson's models, supporting SIRT2 inhibition therapeutically.

nodes.label: α-synuclein-mediated toxicity
nodes.description: AGK2-mediated SIRT2 inhibition prevents deacetylation of α-tubulin and microtubule elements, suppressing aggregation and protecting dopaminergic neuron viability in Parkinson's models. The directionality is AGK2/SIRT2 inhibition upstream of neuronal rescue. This targets the microtubule instability underlying synuclein toxicity. It is a leading SIRT2-inhibition neurodegenerative strategy.

nodes.label: Ischemic stroke
nodes.description:
Ischemic Stroke is acute brain injury caused by focal arterial occlusion — typically thromboembolic — that deprives downstream tissue of oxygen and glucose. It accounts for roughly 85% of all strokes, the remainder being hemorrhagic.

## Etiology & Pathophysiology

- Occlusion mechanisms: large-artery atherosclerosis, cardioembolism (e.g. atrial fibrillation), small-vessel (lacunar) disease, and cryptogenic causes.
- Ischemic core vs. penumbra: the core suffers rapid necrosis from ATP depletion and loss of ion gradients, while the surrounding penumbra is hypoperfused but potentially salvageable — the target of reperfusion therapy.
- Injury cascade: Hypoxia collapses Oxidative Phosphorylation, triggering Excitotoxicity (glutamate-driven calcium influx), Mitochondrial Dysfunction, and a surge of Reactive Oxygen Species. Ischemia-reperfusion Injury adds a secondary oxidative burst upon restored blood flow.

## Clinical Presentation & Management

- Sudden focal deficits (hemiparesis, aphasia, visual loss); diagnosis relies on non-contrast CT/MRI to exclude hemorrhage.
- Standard care: IV thrombolysis (tPA) within the therapeutic window and mechanical thrombectomy for large-vessel occlusion.

## Investigational Neuroprotection

> [!info] Methylene blue rationale
> Methylene blue can act as an alternative electron carrier that bypasses damaged Mitochondrial Electron Transport Chain complexes, sustaining ATP production and lowering Mitochondrial Superoxide. This has motivated its st

nodes.label: SIRT6 centenarian variants (N308K/A313S)
nodes.description: Centenarian-associated SIRT6 variants (N308K/A313S) elevate endogenous SIRT6 protein through a weakened interaction with vimentin, independent of mRNA changes. The directionality is variant → reduced vimentin binding → higher SIRT6. This suggests protein stability, not expression, drives the longevity phenotype. It links a human genetic finding to SIRT6 abundance.

nodes.label: SIRT6 protein levels
nodes.description: Centenarian-associated SIRT6 variants (N308K/A313S) elevate endogenous SIRT6 protein through a weakened interaction with vimentin, independent of mRNA changes. The directionality is variant → reduced vimentin binding → higher SIRT6. This suggests protein stability, not expression, drives the longevity phenotype. It links a human genetic finding to SIRT6 abundance.

nodes.label: SIRT6 N308K mutation
nodes.description: The N308K substitution selectively reduces SIRT6–vimentin interaction, which normally promotes SIRT6 degradation, thereby increasing SIRT6 protein levels. The directionality is N308K upstream of weakened vimentin binding. This stabilizes SIRT6 and enhances its functional output. It is the molecular explanation for the centenarian variant phenotype.

nodes.label: Vimentin
nodes.description: The N308K substitution selectively reduces SIRT6–vimentin interaction, which normally promotes SIRT6 degradation, thereby increasing SIRT6 protein levels. The directionality is N308K upstream of weakened vimentin binding. This stabilizes SIRT6 and enhances its functional output. It is the molecular explanation for the centenarian variant phenotype.

nodes.label: SIRT6 deacetylase activity
nodes.description: Despite higher SIRT6 protein, centenarian hMSCs show increased histone acetylation at H3K9, H3K18, and H3K27, confirming reduced deacetylase activity. The directionality is variant upstream of weaker deacetylation. This indicates the longevity benefit may hinge more on ADP-ribosyltransferase than deacetylase function. It reframes how 'active' SIRT6 should be interpreted.

nodes.label: Replicative senescence (hMSCs)
nodes.description: At late passages, centenarian-variant hMSCs show more Ki67-positive proliferating cells and fewer SA-β-gal-positive senescent cells, demonstrating delayed replicative senescence. The directionality is CentSIRT6 upstream of senescence delay. This is a cellular correlate of exceptional human longevity. It supports SIRT6 as a senescence-modulating factor.

nodes.label: Progerin-induced stress
nodes.description: Centenarian SIRT6 variants ameliorate multiple aging phenotypes in progerin-expressing hMSCs: higher Ki67, reduced SA-β-gal, decreased p16/p21, reduced IL-6, and increased Lamin B1. The directionality is CentSIRT6 upstream of progerin-stress resistance. This shows the variant buffers premature-aging (HGPS) pathology. It ties SIRT6 to laminopathy resilience.

nodes.label: LINE-1 derepression (under progerin stress)
nodes.description: Under progerin-induced stress, centenarian-variant hMSCs better maintain LINE-1 repression, with reduced ORF1p and ORF2p proteins. The directionality is CentSIRT6 upstream of continued LINE-1 silencing. This protects genome integrity against retrotransposition. It connects the ADP-ribosyltransferase gain to repetitive-element control.

nodes.label: AAV-CentSIRT6
nodes.description: AAV-mediated delivery of centenarian SIRT6 reduces LINE-1 ORF1p and ORF2p protein levels in HGPS patient-derived fibroblasts, validating the variant's silencing function in progeria. The directionality is CentSIRT6 expression upstream of LINE-1 reduction. This is a proof-of-concept gene-therapy approach to laminopathy. It extends the SIRT6/LINE-1 axis to a treatable model.

nodes.label: LINE-1 in HGPS fibroblasts
nodes.description: AAV-mediated delivery of centenarian SIRT6 reduces LINE-1 ORF1p and ORF2p protein levels in HGPS patient-derived fibroblasts, validating the variant's silencing function in progeria. The directionality is CentSIRT6 expression upstream of LINE-1 reduction. This is a proof-of-concept gene-therapy approach to laminopathy. It extends the SIRT6/LINE-1 axis to a treatable model.

nodes.label: KAP1
nodes.description:
KAP1 (KRAB-associated protein 1), also known as TRIM28 or TIF1β, is a ubiquitously expressed transcriptional corepressor and member of the tripartite motif (TRIM) family. In senescence and aging, KAP1 is a critical silencer of retrotransposable elements: the deacetylase SIRT6 mono-ADP-ribosylates KAP1, promoting its interaction with the heterochromatin factor HP1alpha to package LINE-1 (LINE-1) elements into repressive heterochromatin.

## Overview

KAP1/TRIM28 contains an N-terminal RBCC/TRIM domain, a central HP1-binding motif, a PHD finger, and a C-terminal bromodomain. It is the universal corepressor for KRAB-zinc-finger transcription factors, recruiting SETDB1 (H3K9 methyltransferase), HDACs, and HP1 to establish H3K9me3-dominated silent chromatin at transposons and endogenous retroviruses.

## Structure & Function

Through its HP1-binding domain and collaboration with SETDB1, KAP1 builds and maintains facultative/repetitive heterochromatin. Its repressive activity is dynamically regulated by post-translational modifications, notably SUMOylation and, in the senescence context, SIRT6-dependent mono-ADP-ribosylation, which enhance its heterochromatinizing function.

## Role in Senescence / SASP

The review places KAP1 on the retrotransposon-derepression axis that drives inflammaging and SASP. RB1 and SIRT6 are enriched at the 5′UTR of LINE-1 loci in proliferating cells, where SIRT6 mono-ADP-ribosylates KAP1, promoting KAP1–HP1α interaction and heterochromatinization of L1

nodes.label: SIRT6/KAP1
nodes.description: SIRT6-mediated mono-ADP-ribosylation of KAP1 recruits HP1α to package LINE-1 retrotransposons into heterochromatin, silencing their expression. The directionality is SIRT6/KAP1 upstream of HP1α tethering. This protects genome stability by containing mobile elements. It explains how SIRT6 loss derepresses LINE-1.

nodes.label: HP1alpha (to LINE-1 heterochromatin)
nodes.description: SIRT6-mediated mono-ADP-ribosylation of KAP1 recruits HP1α to package LINE-1 retrotransposons into heterochromatin, silencing their expression. The directionality is SIRT6/KAP1 upstream of HP1α tethering. This protects genome stability by containing mobile elements. It explains how SIRT6 loss derepresses LINE-1.

nodes.label: TFEB (at K116)
nodes.description: SIRT1 deacetylates TFEB at Lys116, enhancing its nuclear translocation and transcriptional activity to drive the CLEAR autophagic/lysosomal gene program. The directionality is SIRT1 enzymatic activation of TFEB. This promotes lysosomal biogenesis and autophagic flux. It links SIRT1 to the terminal degradative arm of autophagy alongside ULK1/Beclin-1.

nodes.label: BMAL1
nodes.description:
BMAL1 (Brain and Muscle ARNT-Like 1; ARNTL) is a core component of the mammalian circadian clock. It heterodimerizes with CLOCK to bind E-box elements and drive transcription of clock-controlled genes, including NAMPT, the rate-limiting enzyme of the NAD⁺ salvage pathway.

## SIRT1 Regulation

SIRT1 deacetylates and activates BMAL1, coupling cellular metabolic state (NAD⁺ availability) to circadian gene expression. BMAL1 and CLOCK are themselves transcriptional targets amplified by SIRT1 via PGC-1α in the suprachiasmatic nucleus.

> [!info] Source: SIRT1: Protein Roles at the Nexus (Chaqour, 2026)
> In the liver, SIRT1 deacetylates PGC-1α and amplifies the expression of the circadian transcription factors BMAL1 and CLOCK in the suprachiasmatic nucleus of the hypothalamus. A key transcriptional target of BMAL1 and CLOCK is NAMPT, the rate-limiting enzyme in the NAD⁺ salvage pathway, establishing a rhythmic pattern of SIRT1 activation aligned with the circadian cycle.

## Physiological Significance

The SIRT1–BMAL1/CLOCK–NAMPT loop generates circadian NAD⁺ oscillations, gating SIRT1 activity across the day. Age-related SIRT1 decline disrupts this loop and is considered an early hallmark of premature aging linked to metabolic and neurodegenerative diseases.

## Connections

- CLOCK — BMAL1 heterodimer partner in the core circadian clock.

nodes.label: Atg5
nodes.description:
Atg5 (Autophagy-related 5) is a protein essential for the initiation of Autophagy.

## Role in Immune Cells
- Essential for T Cell survival and proliferation.
- Atg5-deficient T cells are incapable of autophagy initiation, which abrogates the differentiation towards a regulatory Foxp3+ phenotype induced by Spermidine.

## Function

Atg5 is conjugated to Atg12 via a ubiquitin-like reaction and complexes with Atg16L1 to form the E3-like ligase for LC3-PE conjugation.

## Documents

- In addition, spermidine can promote differentiation of CD4+ T cells towards a regulatory Foxp3+ phenotype with an anti-inflammatory profile, which was abrogated in Atg5 -deficient T cells that are incapable of autophagy initiation (Carriche et al., 2021).

- Lysosome biogenesis Regulation and functions
- In this case, nuclear translocation of TFEB/TFE3 requires the autophagy regulators Atg5 and Atg9, but the molecular mechanisms remain elusive (Nezich et al., 2015).
